name: Have you created a security controls set relevant to your service?
conditionsText:
The controls selected should take account of:
- service assets
- security risks and vulnerabilities
- technical architecture
- service environment
- applicable security obligations
- relevant security frameworks
- organisational security requirements.
If the standard frameworks do not address a particular security need, the guidance allows appropriate custom processes or controls to be added, with advice from the organisation's security professionals
requirementTitle: Have you created a security controls set relevant to your service?
requirementDescription: Have you turned the selected frameworks into a practical list of security controls that this particular service needs to implement?
why:
Generic frameworks can contain many controls, not all of which will be relevant to every service.
Creating a service-specific controls set helps ensure that security measures are:
- appropriate to the service
- proportionate to its risks
- connected to what needs protecting
- understandable to delivery teams
- capable of being implemented and evidenced
- maintained as the service evolves.
tasks: Have you created a security controls set relevant to your service?

actions.title: Have you created a security controls set relevant to your service?
actions.description:
Create and maintain a documented set of security controls specifically applicable to the service.
• what controls are required
• where the controls came from
• why they are relevant
• what part of the service they apply to
• how they relate to identified risks or requirements
• any service-specific/custom controls needed.
The controls set should also be shared with delivery teams and reviewed when significant functionality or components are added
